rules.title: Application screening fee capped at actual costs and $30 (CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an applicant a screening fee no greater than the actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information plus the reasonable value of time spent. In no case may it exceed $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI increases since January 1, 1998.
rules.key_value: Actual cost, max $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted annually from 1998)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who receive a request to rent residential property from an applicant, including guarantors and cosigners.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt rules governing deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Not applicable where federal or state housing assistance program rules govern fees

rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date shown is for the current amended text (Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, AB 1170, effective January 1, 2026); the $30 cap with CPI adjustment from 1998 predates this amendment.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available now or within a reasonable period of time.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property or their agents charging application screening fees.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date shown is for the current amended text (AB 1170, effective January 1, 2026); this provision may have existed in earlier form.

rules.title: Screening fee allowed only with first-come process or full refund to non-selected applicants
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if, when collecting it, they offer either a process that considers completed applications in order received, with written screening criteria, approving the first qualifying applicant and charging only when an application is actually considered, or a process refunding the full fee to any non-selected applicant within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission, whichever is first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission (refund option); 7-day refund for inadvertent concurrent fees
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property or their agents charging application screening fees.
rules.exemptions: No refund required under the first-come option for applicants denied after consideration for failing the established screening criteria.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:
rules.conflict_note: Effective date taken from the amendment note (Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, AB 1170, effective January 1, 2026); this subdivision appears to reflect the amended text.

rules.title: Itemized receipt for screening fee
rules.requirement: A landlord must give the applicant a receipt for the screening fee itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent, delivered personally, by mail, or by email if agreed. Any portion of the fee not used for authorized purposes must be returned.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property or their agents who collect an application screening fee.
rules.quoted_span: (d) The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date shown is for the current amended text (AB 1170, effective January 1, 2026).

rules.title: Copy of credit report to fee-paying applicant within seven days
rules.requirement: If an applicant paid a screening fee, the landlord must give the applicant a copy of their consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of receiving it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property or their agents who collect an application screening fee.
rules.quoted_span: (f) If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date shown is for the current amended text (AB 1170, effective January 1, 2026).
